full_judgment:
5. Prosecution in support of its case has examined witnesses and tendered one witness, of them, Md Afzal Hossain (PW 1) is the informant, Shakhawat Hossain (PW 2), Md Habibur Rahman (PW 3), Monzur (PW 4) and Md Mir Jahan (PW 5) are the neighbours of the deceased. Md Zahirul Islam (PW 6), Abu Baker Siddique (PW 8) and Liton (PW 15) are declared hostile by the prosecution. Sarwar Hossain (PW 7) is a formal witness of the inquest report. Md Anwar Masud (PW 10), Md Samrat Miah (PW 11), Ratan (PW 12), Shefali Begum (PW 13), Md Abdul Latif (PW 16) and Most Kohinoor Begum (PW 17) are witnesses to prove circumstantial evidence Md Yunus All (PW 14) is a constable who has carried the dead body to the morgue. Md Fazlul Karim (PW 18) is a Magistrate who has recorded the confessional statement of Most Rizia Doli and Taherul Islam Swapon. He has recorded the statements of PWs 16 and 17 under section 164, CrPC. Doctor Enamul Haque (PW 19) has performed autopsy on the dead body and Md Shamsul Huq (PW 20) is the investigating officer of the case. PW 9 has been tendered by the prosecution. 

 13. The learned Additional Sessions Judge on consideration of the evidence on record held that the confessional statement of Rizia Doli, Taherul Islam Swapon and Abdur Razzaque corroborated each other, that in her confessional statement Rizia Doli gave a detailed account of the commission of the crime, that she stated that six knife blows were inflicted on the abdomen of Nazrul Islam which was corroborated by the inquest report Exhibit 3 and the post-mortem report Exhibit 7, that the confessional statements of Taherul Islam and Abdur Razzaque corroborated the inquest report and the post-mortem report, that the investigating officer did not find immoral conduct of the victim and that as the three confessing accused made consistent statements in all material particulars, there was no doubt that accused Rizia Doli in connivance with hired assailants killed her husband and thereby she committed an offence punishable under section 302 of the Penal Code, that Swapon in his confessional statement disclosed his participation in the killing of the victim and thereby he has committed an offence punishable under section 302 of the Penal Code, that the confession of these 3 accused persons, along with the medical evidence, the oral and circumstantial evidence proved that accused Ataul Islam Ripon was one of the hired assailant and thereby he committed an offence under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. 

 14. The learned Advocates appearing for the accused appellants make almost identical submissions. Their contention is that the confessional statements of Rizia Doli and Taherul Islam Swapon have been procured by the police by torture which have subsequently been retracted by them and in that view of the matter these confessional statements cannot be used against them without independent corroborative evidence. It has further been contended that these accused persons have been taken on police remand on repeated occasions and thereafter they have made confessional statements and, as such, it cannot be said that their statements are true and voluntary. It has further been contended that there is no legal evidence on record against Ataul Islam Ripon and his conviction is absolutely illegal. Finally, it has been submitted that the learned Additional Sessions Judge illegally has taken into consideration of the confessional statement of Abdur Razzaque which cannot be used against the appellants. 

 17. There is no eye-witness in this case. The conviction of Rizia Doli and Taherul Islam Swapon is based upon the confessional statements as well as circumstantial evidence. The conviction of Ataul Islam Ripon is based upon the confessional statements of Rizia Doli and Taherul Islam. As observed above, the learned Additional Sessions Judge split up the case of Razzaque for trial under the Children Act. The learned Additional Sessions Judge ought to have tried Taherul Islam Swapon as well under the Children Act if he found Razzaque was a minor below the age of 16 years, inasmuch as, these accused Razzaque and Taherul Islam Swapon and acquitted accused Takiul Islam @ Taki were students of Class-X at the time of occurrence. While recording confessional statements of accused Razzaque and Swapon, they were 15 years old and, therefore, these two accused were of same age at the time of trial of the case. At any event, accused Swapon did not challenge the jurisdiction of his trial with accused Rizia Doli while accused Razzaque challenged the jurisdiction of his trial and accordingly, the leaned Additional Sessions Judge split up the case. 

 19. The prosecution also relies upon the confessional statement of co-accused Swapan and the circumstantial evidence of PWs 16 and 17 in support of the charge on Rizia Doli. The circumstances are that on the fateful day of occurrence, she has gone to PW 16's house for purchasing a pumpkin after dusk, that on her way back home, PW 17 has accompanied her and that Rizia Doli has fainted on seeing the grill of her compound unlocked. The learned Assistant Attorney-General submits this conduct of Doli is a strong circumstance, which suggests that she has the prior knowledge of the incident. We find no reason to draw an adverse inference from her conduct, inasmuch as, this witness in her earlier statement under section 164, CrPC has stated“ তার পরে ডলির বাসায় ঢুকে গেল আমি ঘরের নীচে দাড়িয়ে খাকলাম। তখন লাইট ছিল না । ঘরের দরজা খোলা ছিল। সে দরজা পর্যন্ত যায় । তার পর চিৎকার করছ। তখন সে আবার চিৎকার দিয়া বেহুশ হয়ে যায়।  This statement shows that on reaching at her house Rizia Doli has found the grill and the door of the house are opened and on entering into the house she has fainted. The learned Advocate for accused Doli submits that she has fainted on seeing the dead body of her husband. This submission cannot be said to be without any basis. This statement having been recorded at or near the time of occurrence cannot be ignored and this statement reduces the veracity of the testimony of PW 17 in this regard. The circumstances relied by the prosecution do not support the prosecution rather, the testimony of PW 17 in this regard supports the defence plea. 

 This statement is inculpatory in nature. He has implicated himself along with Rizia Doli, Ripon and Razzak. He has stated that Ripon has inflicted 7/8 knife blows on the abdomen of the deceased and then he cut throat of the victim. The post-mortem report of the victim supports the prosecution case in material particulars. PW 20 found corresponding injuries on the dead body. His confession was recorded on 13-1-1998 and he retracted it on 1-4-1998. He stated that he was subjected to electric shocks 2/3 times every day and as his mental torture was unbearable, he was compelled to make confession. This retraction has been made at a belated stage of making the confession. PW 18 stated that before recording the confessional statement of Swapon, he gave him sufficient time to refresh his memory, that before recording his confession, he examined him and on being satisfied that he was willing to make confession, his confession was recorded. He denied the defence suggestion that the confessional statement was not true or voluntary. After recording confession, PW 18 made an endorsement to the effect that the accused did not complain to him about any torture or ill treatment and that he did not find any injury on his person. We find no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW 18 who is a Magistrate. A retracted confession has nothing to do with the question of it being voluntary nature and its truthfulness if the Court finds that the confession' is true and voluntary. A confession of an accused in respect of a crime that he has perpetrated it is usually the outcome of penitence and remorse and in normal circumstances it is best evidence against the maker. In that view of the matter, we find that the learned Additional Sessions Judge is justified in treating this confession as true and voluntary. 

 21. Accused Ataul Islam Ripon did not make any confession. Accused Taherul Islam Swapon and Rizia Doli implicated him in their confessional statements but we discarded the confessional statement of Rizia Doli as it was neither true nor voluntary. Except the confessional statement of Taherul Islam Swapon there is no other corroborating evidence on record to link him in the incident. The learned Additional Sessions Judge convicted him on the reasoning that Rizia Doli, Taherul Islam Swapon and Razzaque implicated Ataul Islam Ripon in their confessional statements, that the post-mortem report supported the confessional statement of Swapon as regards the injuries inflicted by him on the abdomen of the deceased and that the prosecution was able to prove that he was one of the assailants. 

 22. The learned Additional Sessions Judge has committed a fundamental error in considering the confessional statement of Razzaque, against the appellants, which cannot legally be taken into consideration in this case. Razzaque was not tried jointly with the appellants. Section 30 of the Evidence Act provides that when more persons than one are being tried jointly for the same offence and a confession made by one of such persons affecting himself and some other of such persons, the Court may take into consideration such confession as against such other person as well as against the persons who make such confession." This section makes the confession of a co-accused a relevant fact if he is tried jointly with the other accused. Razzaque, has not been tried with these accused persons; his confession cannot be used against them. In that view of the matter, we find that except the confessional statement of Taherul Islam Swapon there is no other incriminating evidence to connect Ataul Islam Ripon and Rizia Doli in the incident. 

 23. The learned Additional Sessions Judge was wrong in observing that the medical evidence sufficiently corroborated the confessional statement of Swapon, inasmuch as there must be other independent evidence to act upon the confession of co-accused. The medical evidence corroborates the confessional statement so far as accused Swapon is concerned. The consistent views of the superior Courts in this regard are that the confessional statement of one accused will be inadmissible in evidence against another accused in view of section 3 of the Evidence Act. The confession is only one element in the consideration of all the facts proved in the case. It can be put on the scale and weighed with other evidence. If it is capable of belief independently of the confession, then of course it is not necessary to call the confession in aid. These are the views taken in the cases of Bhubani Saha vs King 76 IA (PC) 147, Joygun Bibi vs State 12 DLR (SC) 156 and Amir Hossain vs State, 37 DLR (AD) 139. It has been observed in the case of Atnir Hossain "It should be noted that if the confession of a co-accused is retracted, the position becomes worse so far the other accused is concerned. But as against a co-accused, the evidentiary value of a retracted confession is practically nil and in absence of strong independent evidence it is totally useless." In this case, Swapon retracted his confession and, therefore the evidentiary value of his confession is practically nil as against Rizia Doli and Ripon are concerned. The circumstantial evidence testified by PW 17 was not sufficient to corroborate the confessional statement of Swapon, inasmuch as her testimony was inconsistent with her earlier statement. There is no other circumstantial evidence to link Rizia Doli in the murder of her husband. The circumstances established by the prosecution are not consistent with the guilt of Rizia Doli. Similarly, as regards Ripon, PW 12 did not implicate him that he was in the microbus with Swapon and, therefore, there is no circumstantial evidence to connect him in the incident. 

 24. Therefore, condemned-prisoner Rizia Doli and the convict Ataul Islam Ripon are entitled to get the benefit of doubt as the prosecution has failed to prove the charge against them beyond reasonable doubt. However, we find that the prosecution has been able to prove the charge against accused Taherul Islam Swapon beyond reasonable doubt. It is in evidence on record that Taherul Islam Swapon was barely 15 years of age at the time of commission of offence. Though he did not challenge his trial with Rizia Doli, the materials on record indicated that he was a minor at the time of trial of the case. He along with Abdur Razzaque and Takiul Islam were students of class X during the relevant time. The tender age of the accused is one of the extenuating circumstances to justify lesser sentence and, in that view of the matter, we are of the view that ends of justice would be met if his sentence is reduced to imprisonment for life.
